subject: beetle
reasoning:
I'm planning how to build a stag beetle model using a safe, minimal subset of the SDK's part-building functions, since I can't directly test the API. I'm thinking through how joints and parts should be structured with position and parent relationships.

I'm sketching out a skeleton layout: a root body joint, thorax, head, jaw joints for the mandibles, abdomen, hinged elytra wing cases, and six legs each with hip, knee, and ankle joints, scaling everything in meters around a roughly 7cm real-world beetle size.

Given the uncertain API for rods and joint orientation, I'm deciding to play it safe by manually building cylinder geometries, rotating them with quaternions to point along the right direction, translating to the midpoint, and placing parts with explicit bone assignments rather than relying on unclear helper functions. Now I'm defining the abdomen as a scaled sphere positioned behind the body.

Planning the rest of the body: elytra as brown half-shells on their own bones, a flattened pronotum, a wide head, and mandibles built from chained curved segments mounted on jaw bones with coordinates plotted out point by point to curve forward and inward, ending in tooth spikes near the tips.

Now I'm setting up the antennae as clubbed with three plates at the tip, small black spherical eyes, and leg geometry mapped from hip to knee to foot with femur, tibia, and tarsus segments spaced for a wide stance, feet resting at ground level. I'm also planning to mirror everything left/right using a sign loop and defining the color palette—dark brown, elytra brown, lighter highlight, black, and leg tones.

Now I'm writing the segment-building code that computes direction vectors between joints, builds a quaternion to orient cylinder geometry along that direction, and adds ball-joint spheres at the connections. I'm laying out the skeleton hierarchy—body as root, thorax and head as children, jaws branching off the head, abdomen and elytra attached to the body, and legs parented to the thorax—each with specific offset positions.

Placing small ground-contact spheres at the foot ends and shaping the elytra and abdomen using scaled sphere geometry positioned above the body.
